name: Crucible ForgeFloor Insulated Glove — Pair
description: Elbow-length insulated work gloves in flame-orange split-leather with a quilted thermal lining and a reinforced palm grip pad. The cuff is wide and unlined for fast removal in emergencies. Crucible Industrial stamped in black on the back of each hand, worn to near-illegibility on most pairs.
functionality: Rated to 300°C radiant heat for short-duration exposure; reinforced palm pad provides grip on hot metal stock and slag tools.
what_it_says: You work near fire and you've made your peace with it.
story_hooks: A pair of gloves with chrome-arm cut-outs has been custom-modified — Crucible doesn't make an aug-compatible version, which means someone did this by hand.
The forge floor requires these gloves at all times, but a veteran worker never wears them — and somehow never gets burned.

physical_description.visual_profile: Elbow-length heavy-duty work gloves with a distinctly industrial aesthetic. The flame-orange leather dominates the silhouette, creating high visibility against darker clothing and environments. The wide, unlined cuff gives them a deliberately utilitarian, no-nonsense appearance—designed for speed over style.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed and accommodating through the palm and fingers, with intentional room for layering or hand augmentations. The cuff sits loose and unfitted, allowing quick glove-off in emergencies. The elbow-length cut provides forearm protection without restriction.
physical_description.primary_material: Split-leather exterior in high-visibility flame-orange; quilted synthetic thermal lining beneath for heat resistance and insulation.
physical_description.texture: The split-leather is slightly rough and worn-textured from industrial use, with a matte finish. The quilted interior creates a padded, ribbed appearance visible at the cuff. The reinforced palm grip pad has a tacky, textured surface for tool and material handling.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant flame-orange split-leather with cream or off-white thermal lining visible at the cuff. Black Crucible Industrial stamping on the back of each hand, typically faded and partially worn away on well-used pairs.
physical_description.closures: None—fully pull-on construction with a wide, unlined cuff that slips over the wrist and lower forearm for rapid removal.
distinctive_features: Reinforced palm grip pad in darker material for enhanced traction
Quilted thermal lining visible along the interior cuff edge
Wide, unlined cuff designed for emergency quick-removal
Crucible Industrial manufacturer stamp on the back of each hand, worn nearly illegible on most pairs
Elbow-length coverage extending past the wrist for forearm protection
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 functional workwear. Affordable and practical for working-class industrial labor, not a status item but a necessary tool.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by forge workers, industrial laborers, maintenance technicians, and other hands-on workers in the GLMZ. The garment signals competence, practical experience, and affiliation with manufacturing or infrastructure sectors. Frequently seen on both organic and augmented workers.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn and broken-in. Most pairs show significant scuffing on the orange leather, frayed cuff edges, and the manufacturer stamp worn to near-invisibility. Thermal lining may be slightly compressed. Heavy use is expected and normalized.
